verdict: GM earned $3.3B attributable to stockholders — EPS of $3.73 versus $1.35 a year ago, when results carried heavy special items — on revenue up 3% to $50.0B.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.note: Vehicles and parts — GM North America is the profit center, with segment EBIT-adjusted of $3.6B in the quarter.

segments.name: GM Financial
segments.note: Auto loans and leases for GM buyers and dealers, earning interest and lease revenue.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Automotive selling, general and administrative expense.

otherDetail: Interest income and other non-operating income of $274M, less automotive interest expense of $162M, plus $233M of equity income from joint ventures (folded into the chart's other line, for a total of $345M).
footerNote: The direct-cost block combines automotive and other cost of sales ($40,739M) with GM Financial's interest, operating and other expenses ($3,651M). Automotive revenue is shown net of $3M of eliminations. Net income in the chart is the total of $3,377M; $3,335M was attributable to stockholders and $42M to noncontrolling interests.

takeaways.title: North America did the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: GM North America's EBIT-adjusted rose 43% to $3,592M — pricing and truck/SUV mix — while total EBIT-adjusted rose 22% to $4,106M on revenue up just 3%.

takeaways.title: This year's EPS is clean
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS of $3.73 nearly matches adjusted EPS of $3.70 — unlike a year ago ($1.35 GAAP vs $2.80 adjusted), when special items carved more than half the profit away.

takeaways.title: Guidance narrowed upward
takeaways.text: GM now expects full-year net income attributable to stockholders of $8.9–9.5B and EBIT-adjusted of $14.5–15.5B, with adjusted automotive free cash flow of $11.5–12.5B.
